tools.name: listen_clip

tools.name: get_job_result
tools.description:
Fetch the result of a long transcribe or research call that returned {"status": "running", "job_id"}.
        Call it again every 20 to 30 seconds until status is 'done'; the finished result has the same shape as the
        original tool's. Patchwell settles the call's charge when the job finishes,

tools.name: submit_batch
tools.description:
Queue many items for one tool. They run in parallel at this key's share, each priced exactly like a
        single call (failed and refused items are free). Returns the batch at once; follow it with get_batch, and
        read finished items with get_batch_results while it runs.

tools.name: get_batch
tools.description: A batch's status, progress (done / total), item counts, spend and estimated finish. Free.

tools.name: get_batch_results
tools.description:
Finished items, one per entry: index, custom_id, status and the result (or error). Works while the batch
        runs. Free.

tools.name: cancel_batch
tools.description: Stop starting new items. Items already running finish and are billed; nothing else is charged.

tools.name: clean_data
tools.description:

tools.name: find_tools
tools.description:
Search every Patchwell tool, including those not listed here by name. Returns each match's name, one
        line on what it does and its price. Then describe_tool(name) gives its input, and run_tool(name, input)
        runs it. Free.

tools.name: describe_tool
tools.description:
Everything needed to run one tool: its input as a JSON Schema, options, limits, price and what it
        returns. Pass that input to run_tool. Free.

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description:
Run any Patchwell tool by name, priced and billed exactly as that tool (see its price in find_tools or
        describe_tool; refusals and failures cost nothing). A slow call returns {"status": "running", "job_id"}:
        call get_job_result with it.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "research" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "clean_data" is 1744 chars, far longer than this server's median (244). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

evidence.snippet: Clean a messy spreadsheet or JSON export into typed, deduplicated records with a log of each change. Use it when a spreadsheet or export needs cleaning or dedup…

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "clean_data" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Clean a messy spreadsheet or JSON export into typed, deduplicated records with a log of each change. Use it when a spreadsheet or export needs cleaning or dedup…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: research, submit_batch, clean_data · Private data: transcribe, research, clean_data · Public sink: submit_batch, clean_data · Destructive: submit_batch, describe_tool, run_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: research, submit_batch, clean_data · Private data: transcribe, research, clean_data · Public sink: submit_batch, clean_data · Destructive: submit_batch, describe_tool, run_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "transcribe" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
